changelog.body:
First public release.

**Privacy controls (per app)**
- Location via `LocationManager`: Restrict or Simulate a fixed position
- Wi-Fi network identity: Restrict, or Simulate a stable fake router name and BSSID
- Phone & SIM info: Restrict ("no SIM"), or Simulate a carrier (T-Mobile, Verizon, Vodafone UK, Telekom, Orange)
- Android ID and device model/manufacturer: Simulate, stable per app and rotatable
- Contacts, call log and calendar: Restrict per source (reads return no entries)
- Clipboard reads: Restrict
- Sensors: audit only, or Restrict by group

**App**
- Home with protection status, per-category coverage and a 7-day privacy report
- Templates (Strict, Anti-tracking, Personal data guard, your own) and bulk actions
- Local audit log with filters and JSON/CSV export; optional access notifications
- Backup & restore, Quick Settings kill switch, crash-loop protection
- Light, dark and system themes with dynamic color

**Requirements:** rooted Android 10+ and LSPosed (or a fork such as Vector) with Xposed API 93+.
Add AppGuard itself and each app you want to control to the module scope.

Signing certificate SHA-256: `df1930009ab9ccca5e45d07f45984c0ec75808c3bf9d32219ba02255e5286da6`

readme:
# AppGuard Choose, app by app, what each app can see. AppGuard changes how selected privacy-sensitive Android APIs behave inside the apps you pick. Target APKs are not modified, and nothing leaves your device.

Home
Apps
Policy editor
Network & SIM
## What it controls | Data | Modes | |---|---| | Location (`LocationManager`) | Allow · Restrict · Simulate a fixed position | | Wi-Fi network identity (SSID, BSSID, MAC, local IP, nearby networks) | Allow · Restrict · Simulate a stable fake router | | Phone & SIM (carrier, country, phone number, subscriptions) | Allow · Restrict ("no SIM") · Simulate a carrier | | Android ID and device model/manufacturer | Allow · Simulate (stable per app, rotatable) | | Contacts, call log and calendar | Allow · Restrict per source (reads return no entries) | | Clipboard reads | Allow · Restrict (copy and keyboard paste keep working) | | Sensors (motion, compass, environment, activity, body) | Audit only · Restrict by group | Also included: - **Local audit log** with filters and JSON/CSV export, plus a 7-day privacy report. - **Templates** (Strict, Anti-tracking, Personal data guard, or your own) and bulk actions. - **Backup & restore** of the whole configuration. - **Kill switch** on the home screen and as a Quick Settings tile. - **Access notifications** when a policy blocks something (optional). - **Crash-loop protection**: a policy is suspended automatically if it makes an app crash at start-up. Every hook **fails open**: on any error, missing or corrupt configuration, the app keeps its normal behavior. System and emergency components (phone, SystemUI, Settings, Play services) can never be targeted. ## Requirements - Rooted Android 10+ (tested on Android 14). - LSPosed or a fork such as Vector, with Xposed API 93 or newer. ## Setup 1. Install the APK and enable **AppGuard** in the LSPosed manager. 2. Add **AppGuard itself** and every app you want to control to the module's scope. 3. Open AppGuard, go to **Apps**, pick an app, switch on **Apply policy** and choose modes. 4. Force-stop the target app (the policy page has a button for this) and open it again. ## Limitations AppGuard intercepts the public Java APIs listed above in the app's own process. Native code, Google Play services fused location, server-side fingerprinting and data an app collected earlier are not affected. Each policy page lists exactly what is intercepted and what is not. ## Privacy No network permission, accounts or telemetry. The audit log stays in AppGuard's private storage with bounded retention. Clipboard contents and real identifiers are never logged. ## Source and support Source code, issues and full documentation: https://github.com/imkamaran/AppGuard Licensed under GPL-3.0.
